Review the Service Quotas Console or Service Quotas documentation and be sure that your Guardrails runtime limits are sufficient for your call volume.\\n\\n**What happens if I have both organization-level and account-level enforced guardrails as well as a guardrail in my request?**\\n: All 3 guardrails will be enforced at runtime. The net effect is a union of all guardrails, with the most restrictive control taking precedence.\\n\\n This applies to guardrails enforced at *different levels* \u2014 organization, account, and request. It does not describe multiple Amazon Bedrock policies attached at different points in your organization hierarchy. Those are resolved by AWS Organizations into a single effective policy before enforcement, rather than combined. See the note in Organization-level enforcement.\\n\\n**When should I use selective or comprehensive guarding control?**\\n: Use **Selective** when you trust callers to tag the right content and want to reduce unnecessary guardrail processing. This is useful when callers handle a mix of pre-validated and user-generated content, and only need guardrails applied to specific portions. Use **Comprehensive** when you want to enforce guardrails on everything, regardless of what the caller tags. Accepts specific model identifiers or the keyword `ALL` to explicitly include all models. Create versions of your guardrail when you are satisfied\\nwith a set of configurations.\\n\\nYou can use the test window (for more information,\\nsee Test your guardrail) to compare how different versions of your\\nguardrail perform when evaluating the input prompts and model responses, and generating controlled responses for\\nthe final output. When you use versions, you can switch between different configurations for your guardrail, and update\\nyour application with the most appropriate version for your use case.\\n\\nThe following topics discuss how to create a version of your guardrail when it's ready for deployment, view\\ninformation about it, and delete it when you no longer want to use it.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nGuardrail versions aren't separate resources and don't have their own ARN. A guardrail ARN\\ndoesn't include a version, so the `Resource` element of an IAM policy can't target\\nan individual version. It applies to the guardrail and all of its versions.\\n\\nTo restrict access to a specific guardrail version, use the\\n`bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier` condition key, which accepts the guardrail ARN with an\\noptional `:version` suffix. For more information, see\\nEnforce the use of specific guardrails in model\\ninference requests.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* Create a version of a guardrail\\n* View information about guardrail versions\\n* Delete a version of a guardrail\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-deploy.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"create_guardrail_version\",\"context\":\"Bedrock / Client / create_guardrail_version\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/botocore/latest/reference/services/bedrock/client/create_guardrail_version.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Check Bedrock guardrail version quota in AWS docs"}
